title: Sum of Two Integers: Adding Without a Plus
summary: Add column by column ignoring carries with XOR, find the carries with AND and a shift, and repeat until nothing carries.

analogy.scenario: A counting board with five columns (16, 8, 4, 2, 1) has no '+' key. To add 5 and 7, write each column's sum ignoring carries, then add the carries the same way.

takeaway.summary: x ^ y adds without carries; (x & y) << 1 is the carries. Repeat with the two until the carry is 0.

scenes.narration: A counting board has columns worth 16, 8, 4, 2, and 1, but no plus key. In its columns, 5 is 00101 and 7 is 00111. How do you add them?
scenes.caption: Add 5 and 7 with no plus sign

scenes.narration: You could add 1 seven times, but that takes as many steps as the number. Columns do better: add every column at once, then handle the carries.
scenes.caption: Counting up one at a time takes as many steps as the number

elements.text: One round per carry chain, not per unit

scenes.narration: XOR adds each column but forgets carries: 1 plus 1 leaves 0. AND marks the columns where both are 1, and those carry, so shifting left moves each carry into the next column.
scenes.caption: Round 1: XOR gives 00010, AND shifted left gives carries 01010

scenes.narration: Now add the partial sum and the carries the same way: XOR gives 01000, and one new carry slides into the 4 column.
scenes.caption: Round 2: add 00010 and the carries 01010

scenes.narration: 01000 and 00100 share no column, so XOR adds them completely and nothing carries.
scenes.caption: Round 3: 01000 plus 00100, no columns overlap: carry 0

scenes.narration: With no carry left, the board reads 01100: 12, found with nothing but XOR, AND, and shifts.
scenes.caption: The carry is 0: 5 + 7 = 12

scenes.narration: Columns are bits. XOR is the sum without carries, AND shifted left is the carries; repeat until the carry is zero. At most one round per bit.
scenes.caption: Repeat x ^ y and (x & y) << 1 until the carry is 0
